title: A Signal for the Machine Again
premise: Xanthe Sandoval, a terraformer turned cargo hauler in contested orbits, discovers her name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that was destroyed three years ago with everyone aboard—including the crew she once called family. Someone is broadcasting a signal from a relay at the edge of dead space using the Meridian's codes, and whoever answers it first will control the only navigable corridor through contested territory. Racing rival salvagers and her own grief, Xanthe reaches the relay and finds its caretaker: Ivo, the ship's engineer she believed dead, kept alive by memory-harvesting machines that feed on belonging. To free him, Xanthe must let the machines take her own memories of the crew—the garden, the names, the years—until she chooses instead to overwrite the signal itself, trading her invisibility for a broadcast that carries all their names home. The book ends with Xanthe half-remembering but re-rooted, planting the terraformed garden's first seed beside a man learning to be alive again.
about_author: M. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing shipping manifests before writing stories about the people behind them. They live somewhere with real weather and write about gardens on worlds that don't have any yet.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. While filing routine cargo declarations in the contested Halcyon Drift, Xanthe spots the Meridian—a ship lost three years ago with her entire found family aboard—listed as active, with her own name on tomorrow's manifest. She dismisses it as a clerical ghost, but her hands shake. Emotional beat: the past knocking politely on a door she welded shut.

chapters.title: The Garden for No One
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, flashback-woven. Tending the terraforming greenhouse she inherited from the Meridian's botanist, Xanthe recalls the crew who taught her to belong, and why she vanished into anonymous hauling work afterward. A port official warns her someone has been asking about her by name. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into dread—invisibility was her armor.

chapters.title: Dead Codes
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She traces the manifest anomaly to a repeating transmission on Meridian frequencies originating from Relay Kestrel-9 at the edge of dead space. The codes are authentic—engineer Ivo Reyes' personal cipher, which he never shared. Rival salvager Captain Ondine Voss is also sniffing the signal. Emotional beat: hope arriving like an intruder.

chapters.title: What Ondine Wants
chapters.summary: Ondine Voss's POV. Ambitious and pragmatic, Ondine plans to claim whatever broadcasts from Kestrel-9; a living Meridian survivor or working relay means salvage rights worth a fortune. She offers Xanthe partnership, reading her grief as leverage. Xanthe refuses but realizes Ondine will get there first. Emotional beat: being seen by the wrong person.

chapters.title: Through the Contested Dark
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A tense run through patrol-blockaded corridors, smuggling her small ship past checkpoints using routes only the old crew knew—memory as navigation. She nearly loses everything to a customs interdiction and understands someone flagged her deliberately. Emotional beat: the past as both map and trap.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. She reaches the derelict relay and finds it humming, maintained, warm—and finds Ivo alive inside, older, half-lucid, wired into memory-harvest machines that have been feeding on his recollections of the crew to keep him breathing. He doesn't fully recognize her. Emotional beat: reunion as horror; getting what you wished for, wrong.

chapters.title: The Machines That Keep Us
chapters.summary: Ivo's fragmented POV. Through his dissolving memories we learn the truth: he survived the Meridian's destruction, was rescued by the relay's autonomous systems, and the machines sustained him by consuming his memories—but they're running out of him, and they've been broadcasting to lure more minds. Emotional beat: love measured in what's left to lose.

chapters.title: Ondine Arrives
chapters.summary: Alternating Xanthe/Ondine POV. Ondine docks, intending to strip the relay and sell Ivo's tech; the machines, starved, begin pulling memories from everyone aboard. Xanthe bargains: the machines will release Ivo if given a richer source—one willing mind full of the crew's shared history. Hers. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed as the last way to keep them.

chapters.title: A Signal for the Machine
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, climax. Plugged into the harvest array, Xanthe floods the machines with every memory of the crew—the garden, the jokes, the names—overwhelming them until they release Ivo and go dormant, their purpose fulfilled. She wakes with gaps where her family used to be, holding only the feeling of having loved them. Emotional beat: giving away the treasure to save the person.

chapters.title: First Seed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Xanthe and Ivo return to the greenhouse. She doesn't remember the crew's faces, but Ivo remembers enough for both of them, telling their stories back to her like planting rows. Together they sow the garden's first true seed—meant, at last, for people who will live to see it. Emotional beat: found family rebuilt from fragments; belonging chosen again.
